Finding: Some reported records have no fire name.
Effect on analysis: Q4 cannot show a name for those records; other available fields can still support other questions.
Next action: Investigate whether names can be recovered. Retain usable records for questions that do not need a name.

Finding: Some records have no containment-date value.
Effect on analysis: Q3 cannot calculate duration for these records even when a discovery date is available.
Next action: Seek the missing dates from a reliable source, or define and report a subset with both usable dates.

Finding: Some source rows have the same complete values as other source rows.
Effect on analysis: Repeated reported values may affect Q1 counts and Q2 totals if they represent redundant records.
Next action: Review the matching rows and original source identifiers before deciding whether any record is redundant.

Finding: Outside spaces or unavailable names need attention for the name comparison.
Effect on analysis: Q4 may display or compare equivalent spellings differently; unnamed records still lack a label.
Next action: Review the original and comparison values. Agree a formatting treatment and handle absent names separately.

Finding: Some cause labels do not supply an informative reported cause for the planned comparison.
Effect on analysis: Q2 must explain undefined or unrecognised causes when comparing size across reported causes.
Next action: Review the labels. Keep legitimate undefined causes visible as a separate limitation; do not guess a cause.

Finding: Some containment values are absent or cannot be interpreted using the CSV date format.
Effect on analysis: Q3 cannot use those endpoints. Passing readable values does not recover absent dates.
Next action: Seek reliable date recovery or define a duration subset. Investigate present conversion failures separately.

Finding: Date order or the availability of a usable date pair requires attention.
Effect on analysis: Q3 needs usable endpoints in the stated order. Untested pairs cannot supply a duration under this rule.
Next action: Investigate reversed pairs and unavailable endpoints separately. Define the duration population using both readiness and order.

Finding: Reported-year agreement with discovery year has disagreements or unavailable comparisons.
Effect on analysis: Q1 can assign a record to different annual groups depending on the year field used.
Next action: Review the original field definitions and affected source records before adopting a year field or correcting a value.
